newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian blue chips end lower but index rises.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian blue chips end lower but index rises.

text.p: Nigerian blue chips traded mostly lower at the stock market on Thursday but this did not stop the index rising, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 6515.57 as against 6505.31 on Wednesday.
Dealers said reduced profits of Nigerian Flour Mills and Vitafoam did little to cheer markets.
Flour Mills posted a reduced after-tax profit for the first quarter to-end June while Vitafoam's third quarter result saw declining profits.
Shares of Flour Mills ended unchanged at 10.76 naira. Vitafoam's slumped 10 kobo to 4.90 naira.
Banks and conglomerates shares also fell.
Afribank and United Bank for Africa each closed 10 kobo down at 5.60 naira and 5.05 naira, respectively. NAL Merchant Bank finished five kobo lower at 5.20 naira.
"Demand for their shares was low because investors showed no interest," Mike Itegboje of TRW Stockbrokers said.
Conglomerates UAC was five kobo lower at 10.85 naira while John Holt closed two kobo down at 11.23 naira.
But cement and oil company shares finished higher. Benue Cement added 25 kobo to 5.75 naira, while African Petroleum and National Oil both ended at 31.50 naira, each gaining 30 kobo.
Nestle Foods rose 40 to 31.00 naira while United Textiles, sole gainer in textiles sector, ended 7.10 naira, up 10 kobo.
